correctness.rationale: For any maximizer interior to (0,1), the variational identity gives f(Phi_h(x_h))=f(x_h). A centered half-orbit proves Delta_h tends to 1; the endpoints then give lambda*x_h asymptotic nu*(1-y_h). Comparing T(y_h)-T(x_h)=h using convergent C2 endpoint logarithmic renormalizations yields the exact kappa and C_f for all maximizers. The finite-h mu_h max formula follows from the previously published scalar barrier proposition. Logistic, cubic and a distinct fixed-slope family were separately checked with CHECK.py; these numerical calculations do not prove the general statement.

originality.rationale: The inspected source proves the exact maximum-displacement identity and gives the exact cubic sample but analyzes the small-sampling limit. The new theorem instead proves a universal large-sampling law for arbitrary smooth repeller-to-sink scalar flows, a transit-time-dependent coefficient and sharp optimizer endpoint locations. Searches for a dominating or equivalent older large-h general statement did not produce one; this is a best-knowledge originality finding, not certification of historical priority.

value.rationale: The recently introduced sampled intensity quantifies resistance to persistent bounded kicks. Existing sampling theory emphasizes h down to zero. The long-h regime is mathematically natural for coarse observations: tolerance saturates at the basin width with a nontrivial exponent coupling unstable and stable timescales and a computable global transit-time prefactor. The explicit family with identical endpoint eigenvalues but varying C_f demonstrates information beyond local linearization. The result applies uniformly to the natural infinite-dimensional class of all C2 scalar f satisfying the hypotheses, not an arbitrary isolated numeric example.
